Bounded actual SH-4 FA29 collector and drawn-window instruction cost.

KOS IRQ save/restore instructions execute unchanged with architectural SR
state; no IRQ stubs or new assembly are used. Every production executable
section must equal the address-metadata fixture section before timing.
Warm/cold-I cycles use the existing perfect-D-cache scheduling model. Data
lines are 32-byte touched addresses, not measured misses or console latency.

1.value:
Price actual dynamic instruction traces with the repository's hwsim model.

Perfect caches, no memory/bus/SQ/DMA events and no final completion drain.
This is a synthetic CPU scheduling comparison, never hardware time or FPS.

2.value:
Observe real opcode data accesses without inventing cache misses.

Instruction fetches are excluded; PC-relative literal loads are data loads.
The fixture maps cached RAM at low synthetic addresses, which become the
0x8c000000 alias only for the pipeline-model ELF. Distinct 32-byte lines are
working-set/touch counts, not measured fills or hardware bus transactions.

3.value: PREF requests observed separately; not demand loads, fills or guaranteed useful transfers

4.value: Initially cold 8KB I-cache, once per complete sequence; synthetic ELF layout

5.value: Isolated instruction segment after the mask is installed through its restore instruction; model scheduling starts at this segment. It is not hardware interrupt latency.

6.value: Entry-to-return callee instructions, including actual KOS inline IRQ mask/restore and linked toolchain memcpy/memset. Caller argument setup/call instruction, optional weak actor-reset callback, formatting, QA transport, thread scheduling, interrupt delivery, D-cache misses and real gap event frequencies are excluded. All window instructions observed with IRQ mask clear. Protected-region timings start from an isolated model pipeline and are not measured interrupt latency. Local per-slot/probe counter accumulation at gap hooks is not in the common hit cost. Scenarios assume 1000 or10000 events and30ms other work; no frame-speedup prediction. Cold-I costs are isolated and cannot be summed into a frame. No private data, full image or console result.
